## Parametric and Nonparametric Statistical Test Analysis

The purpose of this report is to analyze the power and effect sizes of the parametric analysis of variance (ANOVA) and nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis statistical test, as well as discuss the most appropriate use of each test accordingly in different scenarios.

## Running Code

The following charts compares the Type 1 error rates of the parametric ANOVA and nonparametric KW test under different scenarios for effect size β=0.

```{r}
#| label: default
#| echo: false
 
set.seed(1)
conf <- config::get(config="default")

anovaset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)
kwset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)

for (w in seq_len(conf$iterations)){
  
  
  anovaset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  kwset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  
  for (c in seq_len(conf$simulations)){
    
    
    #control group negative
    data <- lapply(seq_len(conf$groups), function(u){
      if (conf$condition=="normal"){
        rnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      } else if (conf$condition=="skewed") {
        rlnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      }
    }
    )
    
    
    raw <- unlist(data)
    groups <- factor(rep(1:conf$groups, each = conf$sample))
    
    df <- data.frame(
      values = raw,
      group = groups
    )
    
    #tests
    
    
    results <- oneway.test(
      values ~ group,
      df,
      var.equal=TRUE
    )
    pVal <- results$p.value
    
    anovaset2[c] <- pVal
    
    results_kw <- kruskal.test(
      values ~ group,
      data = df,
    )
    
    pVal_kw <- results_kw$p.value
    
    kwset2[c] <- pVal_kw
    
    
    
  }
  
  anova_reject_proportion <- (sum(anovaset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  kw_reject_proportion <- (sum(kwset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  
  anovaset1[w] <- anova_reject_proportion
  kwset1[w] <- kw_reject_proportion
}

print("Simulations are finished!")
print(anovaset1)
print(kwset1)

# -- Plot --

plot(density(anovaset1),col=rgb(0,0,1), 
     xlim=c(0, 1), 
     ylim=c(0,conf$iterations),
     
     xlab=
       if (conf$reject=="No"){
         "Proportion of Type I Error"
       } else {
         "Power of the test"
       },
     ylab="Density",
     main=conf$title
     )

lines(density(kwset1), col=rgb(1,0,0,))
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend= c("ANOVA", 
            "Kruskal-Wallis"),
  col= c("blue", "red"),
  pch= c(16,16)
)
```

The following charts compare the power of the parametric ANOVA and nonparametric KW test under different scenarios as well as exploring effect size β.

Normal, Reject

```{r}
#| label: reject001
#| echo: false
 
set.seed(1)
conf <- config::get(config="reject001")

anovaset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)
kwset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)

for (w in seq_len(conf$iterations)){
  
  
  anovaset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  kwset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  
  for (c in seq_len(conf$simulations)){
    
    
    #control group negative
    data <- lapply(seq_len(conf$groups), function(u){
      if (conf$condition=="normal"){
        rnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      } else if (conf$condition=="skewed") {
        rlnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      }
    }
    )
    
    
    raw <- unlist(data)
    groups <- factor(rep(1:conf$groups, each = conf$sample))
    
    df <- data.frame(
      values = raw,
      group = groups
    )
    
    #tests
    
    
    results <- oneway.test(
      values ~ group,
      df,
      var.equal=TRUE
    )
    pVal <- results$p.value
    
    anovaset2[c] <- pVal
    
    results_kw <- kruskal.test(
      values ~ group,
      data = df,
    )
    
    pVal_kw <- results_kw$p.value
    
    kwset2[c] <- pVal_kw
    
    
    
  }
  
  anova_reject_proportion <- (sum(anovaset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  kw_reject_proportion <- (sum(kwset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  
  anovaset1[w] <- anova_reject_proportion
  kwset1[w] <- kw_reject_proportion
}

print("Simulations are finished!")
print(anovaset1)
print(kwset1)

# -- Plot --

plot(density(anovaset1),col=rgb(0,0,1), 
     xlim=c(0, 1), 
     ylim=c(0,conf$iterations),
     
     xlab=
       if (conf$reject=="No"){
         "Proportion of Type I Error"
       } else {
         "Power of the test"
       },
     ylab="Density",
     main=conf$title
     )

lines(density(kwset1), col=rgb(1,0,0,))
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend= c("ANOVA", 
            "Kruskal-Wallis"),
  col= c("blue", "red"),
  pch= c(16,16)
)
```

```{r}
        rlnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      }
    }
    )
    
    
    raw <- unlist(data)
    
    df <- data.frame(
      values = raw,
      group = groups
    )
    
    #tests

      df,
      var.equal=TRUE
    )
    pVal <- results$p.value
    
    anovaset2[c] <- pVal
    
    results_kw <- kruskal.test(
      values ~ group,
      data = df,
    )
    
    pVal_kw <- results_kw$p.value
    
    kwset2[c] <- pVal_kw
    
    
    
  }
  
  anova_reject_proportion <- (sum(anovaset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  kw_reject_proportion <- (sum(kwset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  
  anovaset1[w] <- anova_reject_proportion
  kwset1[w] <- kw_reject_proportion
}

       },

legend(

  legend= c("ANOVA",

  col= c("blue", "red"),
  pch= c(16,16)
)
```

```{r}
plot(density(anovaset1),col=rgb(0,0,1), 
     xlim=c(0, 1), 
     ylim=c(0,conf$iterations),
     
     xlab=
       if (conf$reject=="No"){
         "Proportion of Type I Error"
       } else {
         "Power of the test"
       },
     ylab="Density",
     main=conf$title
     )

lines(density(kwset1), col=rgb(1,0,0,))
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend= c("ANOVA", 
            "Kruskal-Wallis"),
  col= c("blue", "red"),
  pch= c(16,16)
)

```

```{r}
#| label: low_n_2_false
#| echo: false
 
set.seed(1)
conf <- config::get(config="low_n_2_false")

anovaset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)
kwset1 <- numeric(conf$iterations)

groups <- factor(rep(1:conf$groups, each = conf$sample))

for (w in seq_len(conf$iterations)){
  
  
  anovaset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  kwset2 <- numeric(conf$simulations)
  
  for (c in seq_len(conf$simulations)){
    
    
    #control group negative
    data <- lapply(seq_len(conf$groups), function(u){
      if (conf$condition=="normal"){
        rnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      } else if (conf$condition=="skewed") {
        rlnorm(conf$sample, unlist(conf$miu[u]), unlist(conf$sd[u]))
      }
    }
    )
    
    
    raw <- unlist(data)
    
    df <- data.frame(
      values = raw,
      group = groups
    )
    
    #tests
    
    
    results <- oneway.test(
      values ~ group,
      df,
      var.equal=TRUE
    )
    pVal <- results$p.value
    
    anovaset2[c] <- pVal
    
    results_kw <- kruskal.test(
      values ~ group,
      data = df,
    )
    
    pVal_kw <- results_kw$p.value
    
    kwset2[c] <- pVal_kw
    
    
    
  }
  
  anova_reject_proportion <- (sum(anovaset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  kw_reject_proportion <- (sum(kwset2<0.05))/conf$simulations
  
  anovaset1[w] <- anova_reject_proportion
  kwset1[w] <- kw_reject_proportion
}


# -- Plot --

t_statistic <-t.test(anovaset1, kwset1)

plot(density(anovaset1),col=rgb(0,0,1), 
     xlim=c(0, 1), 
     ylim=c(0,conf$iterations),
     
     xlab=
       if (conf$reject=="No"){
         "Proportion of Type I Error"
       } else {
         "Power of the test"
       },
     ylab="Density",
     main=conf$title
     )

lines(density(kwset1), col=rgb(1,0,0,))
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend= c("ANOVA", 
            "Kruskal-Wallis"),
  col= c("blue", "red"),
  pch= c(16,16)
)
```
